title: Bloom-prefilter + Deferred Span Resolution to Cut Tracing Hotpath Cost
creator: Ava Morales
description: Background: tracer hotpath allocation and CPU on our ingress services is a top contributor to tail latency. Current sampling decisions consult multiple heuristics and do span encoding on the request thread, which increases P99 latency when QPS spikes. Proposal: introduce a lightweight bloom-prefilter on the hotpath to cheaply identify candidates worth fuller span capture, and defer span resolution/encoding to a bounded async resolver. Combine this with a small in-memory reservoir that preserves rare outliers (error/tail events) so we don't lose actionable traces.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath CPU for tracing reduced by >= 40% under 2k RPS synthetic workload (same sampling rate).
End-to-end P99 latency for ingress service improves by >= 6% in staging perf runs.
No loss of high-value traces: error-tagged traces observed in prod-like replay are retained >= 99% of the time versus baseline.
New sampler is togglable via feature flag and has telemetry showing prefilter accept/reject ratios and async queue depth.
Implementation has unit tests for bloom logic, async handoff, and reservoir eviction policy.
Document rollout plan and rollback steps in the playbook section of the PR.
technical_notes: Bloom filter parameters tuned for per-worker 100k RPS equivalent; target FPR ~0.2% at 1MB memory per worker.
Prefilter checks: presence of error flags, long tail hints (latency bucket from request headers), and lightweight content hashes; only if prefilter indicates 'maybe' do we allocate per-span buffers.
Deferred resolution: span encoding and attribute enrichment moved to a bounded async worker pool. Synchronous path emits a compact placeholder and a sampling hint to the worker.
Reservoir: fixed-size circular buffer per-tenant keeps candidate outliers with a simple rank by latency+error_score; replacements happen in background to avoid hotpath locks.
Backpressure: when async queue is saturated we return to probabilistic sampling with a tenant-aware decay factor and emit metric 'tracer.prefilter.throttle'.
plan: Spike: implement prototype of bloom-prefilter and async resolver in a sandbox service (Liam) — 2 days.
Bench: run synthetic load tests against instrumented ingress with current and new sampler to measure CPU/latency — 3 days (Ops + SRE support).
Iterate: tune bloom parameters and reservoir thresholds based on bench data — 2 days.
PR: open RFC + implementation PR, include metrics dashboard panels and feature flag toggles — 2 days.
Staging rollout: gradual ramp via feat flag by tenant (10%, 30%, 100%) with rollback coupling — 3 days.
Post-mortem: collect regressions and finalize runbook — 2 days.
risks: False negatives in prefilter could drop informative traces if reservoir thresholds are misconfigured.
Async handoff introduces eventual consistency; causal relationships in traces might be weaker if resolution is delayed.
Memory footprint increase per worker for bloom structures if mis-sized; must cap and add auto-tuning.
Edge cases with very short-lived requests may not produce enough signal for prefilter and could be oversampled or lost.
